newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu says PLO trying to scare Israelis.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu says PLO trying to scare Israelis.

text.p: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Tuesday accused the PLO of trying to scare the Israeli public by creating the impression of a united, hostile Arab front against the Jewish state.

Netanyahu said there were suspicions the Palestinian Authority was trying to acquire missiles, weapons not specified for it under peace accords that set up PLO self-rule in parts of the West Bank and Gaza.

He repeated his charge that a deal on handing over parts of the West Bank town of Hebron to the Palestine Liberation Organisation (PLO) could be concluded swiftly, if only the PLO would stop delaying in hopes of pressuring Israel.

"They are trying also to unite the Arab world and via that to scare the Israeli public, to cause people to believe that we really can't defend ourselves, that there will be a war here any minute," Netanyahu told Israel's Army radio in an interview.
Asked by the interviewer to confirm reports that the Authority was trying to arm itself with anti-tank and anti- aircraft missiles, Netanyahu said there were such suspicions.
"There are suspicions they are attempting to equip themselves in different areas. We are watching this," he said.
Asked if he could be more specific, Netanyahu, said:
"There is certain information. I do not want to spread it around here but certainly we are following all these things."
The Palestinian Authority denied it was seeking missiles.

"There is no truth to the Israeli claims that the Palestinian Authority is arming itself with anti-tank and anti- helicopter missiles. This is completely false," Tayeb Abdel- Rahim, secretary-general of the Authority, told Reuters.
"We came here with an agreement which specifies the weapons our security forces will have. The weapons we have are all mentioned in the PLO-Israel peace deal."
